title: Field-level pseudonymization and consent-tag propagation for usage pipelines
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a field-level pseudonymization layer and consent-tag propagation through the streaming analytics pipeline used by the Console backend. Goal is to ensure tenant and user identifiers, email addresses, API keys, and other sensitive fields are pseudonymized or removed before they are persisted to downstream analytics stores (warehouse, cold storage, observability indexes). Consent metadata (consent_granted, consent_scope, consent_ts) must travel with each event so retention and deletion workflows can be applied accurately. This work spans the event ingress transformer, schema registry mappings, low-latency streaming transforms, backfill/repair tooling, and audit trail instrumentation.
acceptance_criteria: A streaming transform stage exists in the ingestion pipeline that applies field-level pseudonymization rules by schema version with pluggable strategies: hash-with-salt (KMS-backed), irreversible wipe, or tokenization reference ID.
Consent tags are attached or normalized for all incoming events and are present as structured metadata through to the warehouse and observability indexes.
Downstream consumers can opt into receiving pseudonymized vs. raw attributes via agreed routing policies; by default raw PII is never stored in analytics topics or materialized views.
End-to-end tests and canary verification show <1% additional ingestion latency and no drop in throughput for the usual peak traffic profile.
A repair/backfill job is available to reprocess historical events for tenants that opt into enhanced pseudonymization, with safe windowing and throttling controls.
Audit logs record which transformation strategy was applied per-event and link to a unique transformation-job-id for regulatory audits.
Documentation for configuration, schema mappings, and operational runbooks exists in Confluence and is linked from the ticket.
Security review sign-off completed and KMS integration verified for salt management.
Rollout plan created with traffic percentage ramps and rollback criteria defined.
technical_notes: We will add a streaming transformer in the Kafka/KS pipeline (ingress topic -> transform -> analytics topic). The transformer is schema-aware via schema-registry v2 and uses a per-tenant policy table.

Pseudonymization strategies: SHA-256 HMAC with KMS-managed per-tenant salt (preferred for deterministic joins), irreversible redact for sensitive free-text fields, and reference tokenization for fields requiring reversible lookup (tokens stored in a secure token vault service).
Consent-tag model: {consent_status, consent_scope, consent_timestamp, source}. Tags are normalized at ingress and must be immutable once stamped to ensure correct retention semantics.

We will add a small metadata header to messages: transformation_version, transformer_id, transformation_strategy, and transformation_job_id. These headers are strings attached to Kafka messages and must be propagated.

Backfill approach: controlled reprocessing with TTL checks. Use existing reprocessing cluster with rate limiter and per-tenant concurrency caps. Backfill must record mapping of original offsets to new offsets for traceability.
Compatibility: provide a compatibility shim so downstream consumers expecting raw attributes can read from a separate mirrored topic with strict RBAC checks and audit logging.
tasks: Design policy table schema for per-tenant pseudonymization rules and consent windows (PM/Legal input required)
Implement streaming transformer microservice with schema-registry integration and KMS salt lookup
Add message header propagation for transformation metadata
Integrate token vault API for reversible tokenization when required
Create unit/integration tests and latency benchmarking harness
Build backfill/repair job with safety throttles and dry-run mode
Create migration scripts to stamp consent-tags for existing producers where feasible
Write runbook: failures, alerting thresholds, on-call playbook
Coordinate security review and KMS/HSM credential rotation plan
Prepare Confluence design doc and demo for GDPR/CCPA compliance team
comments: 2026-01-12 - Ava Martinez: Initial write-up and scope. Open questions: do we require deterministic pseudonyms for cross-table joins? Legal prefers deterministic for certain audit flows, but it increases correlation risk.
2026-01-20 - Ravi Nair: Prototype SHA-256 HMAC with per-tenant salt. Measured negligible CPU overhead on small batch, need to benchmark at 10k rps.

2026-02-02 - Priya Shah (Legal): Consent model approved for initial rollout: consent_scope levels S1,S2,S3. S1 allows aggregated metrics only; S2 allows pseudonymized joins; S3 allows raw attributes for flagged research tenants.
2026-02-15 - SRE (Jordan Li): Willing to provision a canary transform cluster in us-west-2. Need the transformer to expose Prometheus metrics (latency_histogram, processed_count, drop_count).

2026-02-28 - Ravi Nair: Implemented header propagation and transformation metadata logging. Pushed branch ENG-21901/transformer with unit tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1742
2026-03-05 - QA (Maya Chen): Found an edge case where JSON payloads with deeply nested free-text fields bypass redaction. Added task to extend schema-aware traversal to depth 6 and add fuzzing tests.
2026-03-10 - Ravi Nair: Security review requested. Linked Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/infra/pages/Field+Pseudonymization+Design
notes: Prefer deterministic HMAC with KMS per-tenant salts for the first phase to enable safe joins in pseudonymized datasets. Phase 2 may introduce token vault reversible tokens for customer-requested re-identification under strict legal controls. Ensure each step adds audit metadata for regulatory evidence.
